correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the unrestricted Gram argument: rim vector average m and deviations w_i sum to zero; min adjacency eigenvalue of C_n is -2c_n, hence sum rim pair products >=n[(1+c_n)||m||²-c_n]. With a=<z,m>, ||m||²>=a² and spoke term nt a, optimize the resulting quadratic on [-1,1]. Fourier vectors with θ=π (even) or π-π/n (odd) and hub axis realize equality in dimension three for all real t>=0, proving the SDP formula. Fixed-k integer sign count 2min(k,n-k)+tk gives the piecewise cut. Factored exactness polynomials, discriminant and monotone ratio-derivative numerator reduce the universal gap maximum to t=0 vs 2; endpoint inequality yields n=3,5,7 versus odd>=9. Independent cut enumeration and explicit Fourier-Gram PSD/objective checks confirmed 80 sample pairs over n=3..10 and t=0,1,2,3,5, with exact boundary checks at n=3. The case n=3,t=1 isolated exactness was checked. Finite tests corroborate, analytic eigenvalue/derivative proof covers every n,t.

originality.rationale: Qualified PASS with material historical risk: Goemans–Williamson 1995 defines the exact basic SDP; Laurent–Varvitsiotis 2011 treats a different graphwise Grothendieck ratio over arbitrary signed quadratic edge weights, not the t-indexed nonnegative Max-Cut ratio. Ben-Ameur–Glorieux–Neto 2016 full text Table 1 numerically computes basic SDP0 for unweighted wheels t=1 and proposes stronger SDP3; those numerical wheel values are prior work and not claimed novel. Delorme–Poljak 1993 specifically studies wheel-relevant eigenvalue max-cut bounds and is a plausible equivalent predecessor; open and OA attempts found no material full text, and the authorized institutional service returned vpn_disconnected. No conclusion of whole-paper noncoverage is made, but available information does not establish a dominating weighted-wheel theorem.

value.rationale: The basic Max-Cut SDP integrality gap is a natural algorithmic quality measure. A closed all-rim-size one-parameter exactness classification, the exceptional four-vertex wheel exact point and a strictly unique worst spoke weight with a seven-to-nine odd-rim switch quantify relaxation quality in a motivated graph family, beyond a fixed unweighted benchmark.

limitations: Only basic GW relaxation with nonnegative uniform spokes and unit rim edges, not strengthened SDP3 or inhomogeneous signed weights.
